name: Gujarati Khichdi
subtitle: soft rice and moong dal cooked to a porridge, eaten with kadhi and ghee

ingredients.note: four parts liquid to one of grain, by volume
half in the pot, half poured over at the table
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rinse the rice and dal together in three changes of water until it runs clear, then soak 20 minutes and drain.
This khichdi is deliberately soft and loose. The grains should surrender, not stay separate. Do not cut the water.
Have the kadhi made and hot before the khichdi is done; khichdi stiffens fast as it sits.

steps.text: Heat half the ghee in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds until they turn a shade darker.
Add the asafoetida, ginger and green chilli and let them sizzle 10 seconds.
Tip in the drained rice and dal and stir 2 minutes until every grain is glossed with ghee.
steps.tip: This brief fry keeps the khichdi from turning to glue.

steps.text: Add the water, turmeric and salt and stir well, scraping the base.
Close the cooker and cook for 4 whistles on medium heat, then let the pressure fall on its own.
Open, whisk briefly and thin with hot water if it has set firm. It should slump off a spoon.
steps.tip: Only hot water. Cold water added to hot khichdi makes it gluey.

steps.text: Crack the black pepper over, pour the remaining ghee on top and serve with kadhi.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. It sets solid when cold; reheat in a pan with a generous splash of hot water, breaking it up with a spoon.
